what_worked: Four-quadrant capital allocation framework on Slide 6 ties geographic and category findings into actionable recommendations.
fix_next: Reconcile total revenue (~$15.6M not $13.5M), disclose 274 missing categories and 288 missing audience types before making segment claims.
verdict: Polished template with a coherent thesis, undermined by multiple revenue errors and undisclosed missingness.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: Total MRR stated $13.5M vs reference $15.6M (~$2M undercount). Slide 2: AI shown $1,806K vs reference $2,357K; Marketing $444K vs $1,317K; E-commerce $396K vs $1,112K; SaaS $589K vs $704K. Slide 3: US $7,504K implies ~56% share but reference total is higher so share is overstated; title says 'Category Portfolio Matrix' but content is geographic. Slide 4: B2B 2.6x multiple vs reference median multiples ~2.3x; company counts (401+255+56=712) leave 288 unaccounted without disclosure.

evidence.insight: Slide 5 whitespace identification (Customer Support 80% growth, Recruiting 83%) is genuinely useful but built on n=5 and n=6 samples with no confidence caveat. Slide 6 quadrant framework synthesizes findings but recommendations are generic.
evidence.narrative: Arc from market snapshot through geography, business model, whitespaces to roadmap is logical. However Slide 3 title promises 'Category Portfolio Matrix & Investment Quadrants' but delivers geographic analysis—a sequencing break that confuses the reader.
evidence.framing: Audience (internal investment review) and scope (1,000 companies) are set on Slide 1. Critical missingness—274 categories, 288 audience types, 241 countries, 216 zero-revenue rows—is never disclosed, fatally weakening category and B2B/B2C claims. '65 Countries' ignores 241 missing values.
evidence.accuracy: Total revenue understated by ~$2M. At least five category-level revenue figures are materially wrong (AI, Marketing, E-commerce, SaaS, Analytics). B2B/B2C 2.6x multiplier doesn't match reference medians (~2.3x). Brazil 65% growth and Singapore 44% growth are unverifiable and based on tiny samples presented without sample sizes.
evidence.visual: Dark theme is consistent and typography is readable. Bar charts on Slides 2-3 are clean choices. Slide 3 bar proportions are misleading—France bar appears nearly as long as US despite 8x smaller value. Card layouts on Slides 4-6 are clear but template-repetitive.
evidence.ai_slop: Heavy consulting jargon throughout: 'Scale Anchor,' 'B2B Premium,' 'High Momentum,' 'Growth-Share Read.' Slide 6 quadrant labels (Harvest & Defend, Double Down, Selective Bets, Build New) are generic BCG-matrix language that could fit any dataset.

change_reason: Removed 1-point bonus: the strategic framework, while structured, relies on materially incorrect figures and undisclosed missingness, and consulting-template language does not constitute work beyond the rubric. Core dimension scores confirmed as appropriate.
